description:
You are a Database Security and Compliance Administrator at a healthcare services company. Following a regulatory audit, your organization has been required to implement a compliant PII storage system: sensitive data (Social Security Numbers) must be encrypted at rest using industry-standard symmetric key encryption, and every data modification must be automatically captured in an immutable audit log.

Using Azure Data Studio connected to the local SQL Server, implement this compliance system in a NEW dedicated database named 'ComplianceDB'. The system must include:

- A 'ComplianceDB' database with an 'audit' schema
- SQL Server certificate-based AES-256 symmetric key encryption infrastructure: a DATABASE MASTER KEY protected by the password 'Compliance@Secure2024', a certificate named 'AuditDataCert', and a symmetric key named 'SSNEncryptionKey' using AES_256 algorithm encrypted by that certificate
- A sensitive data table 'audit.SensitiveEmployeeData' that stores encrypted SSNs as VARBINARY alongside plaintext demographic fields (FirstName, LastName, DateOfBirth) and metadata (created timestamp, creating user)
- An audit log table 'audit.AuditLog' that records each DML event with its type, affected table name, affected record ID, performing user, timestamp, and additional context
- A stored procedure 'audit.usp_InsertSensitiveRecord' (accepting @SSN, @FirstName, @LastName, @DateOfBirth) that encrypts the SSN using ENCRYPTBYKEY before inserting into the sensitive data table
- An AFTER INSERT trigger on audit.SensitiveEmployeeData that automatically writes one row to audit.AuditLog for each insert
- Three test records inserted via the stored procedure using these identities: Alice Johnson (SSN 123-45-6789, DOB 1985-03-15), Robert Martinez (SSN 987-65-4321, DOB 1979-11-28), Carol Thompson (SSN 456-78-9012, DOB 1992-07-04)

When complete: ComplianceDB must exist with the audit schema; the encryption objects (master key, certificate, symmetric key) must be present; both tables must exist; the stored procedure and trigger must be in place; audit.SensitiveEmployeeData must have 3 rows with non-NULL VARBINARY data in SSN_Encrypted; and audit.AuditLog must have 3 rows confirming the trigger fired.

metadata.application: Azure Data Studio + Microsoft SQL Server 2022
metadata.dataset: No external dataset — agent creates encryption infrastructure and test data from scratch
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Requires creating a new database, schema, certificate-based symmetric key encryption (AES_256), ENCRYPTBYKEY/DECRYPTBYKEY SQL Server APIs, AFTER INSERT trigger with inserted pseudo-table, stored procedure with OPEN/CLOSE SYMMETRIC KEY, and verification that encryption produced non-NULL VARBINARY data. Multiple interdependent objects must be created in the correct order.
